questions.question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence.

Uluru is the world's largest monolith and Australia's recognisable natural icon with an elliptical shape and a circumfarence of around 94 kilometers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Circumfarence**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Circumfarence"** is incorrectly spelled in the sentence. The correct spelling is **"Circumference"**. (परिधि)

 
 
• **Example:** The circumference of the Earth is about 40,075 kilometers.
 
 
 
• **"Circumference"** refers to the distance around a circular or rounded object. (परिधि)
 
 
• **Example:** We measured the circumference of the tree trunk for our science project.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Circumfarence**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Elliptical** (अंडाकार): Shaped like an ellipse, an elongated circle.

 
 
• **Example:** The planet's orbit is elliptical, not perfectly circular.
 
 
 
• **Monolith** (एकाश्म): A large single upright block of stone, especially one shaped into or serving as a pillar or monument.
 
 
• **Example:** The ancient monoliths still stand tall after thousands of years.
 
 
 
• **Kilometers** (किलोमीटर): A metric unit of measurement equal to 1,000 meters.
 
 
• **Example:** The marathon race covers a distance of 42 kilometers.

questions.question:
Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence to make it grammatically correct.

This almirah is made up of __heavier __metal.
questions.solution:
The correct option to substitute the underlined word is **'4'** i.e. **heavy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• "Heavier" is a comparative adjective and is used to compare two items.
 
• Since the sentence does not compare the almirah to another object, the base form "heavy" is appropriate.

The other options contain the following errors:

 
• Option 1: "Heaviest" is a superlative adjective and is used to compare more than two items.
 
• Option 2: "Most heavier" is grammatically incorrect as "heavier" is already a comparative form and does not need "most."
 
• Option 3: "Most heaviest" is grammatically incorrect as "heaviest" is already a superlative form and does not need "most."

**Correct sentence:** *This almirah is made up of heavy metal*.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error in phrasal verb.

Tara was late for the meeting / but somehow managed / to catch out with / everything she had missed.

options.text: Tara was late for the meeting

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. to catch out with .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct phrasal verb in this context should be **“catch up with”** rather than “catch out with.”
 
• “Catch up with” means to reach someone or something by moving faster, or to reach the same level or standard as someone or something else.
 
• The sentence should be corrected to maintain proper usage of the phrasal verb and convey the intended meaning clearly.

Correct sentence: *Tara was late for the meeting but somehow managed to **catch up with** everything she had missed*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Commonly Confused Phrasal Verbs:**

 
 
• **Catch on:** To understand or realize something. *It took him a while to catch on to the joke.*
 
• **Catch out:** To unexpectedly find out something, often a mistake. *The teacher caught the student out in a lie.*
 
• **Catch up:** To reach the same level or position as others. *She had to stay late to catch up on her work.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Never _______ ever seen a more disgusting sight.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**Have I**" is the correct phrase to use in inverted word order for emphasis, which is common in English.
 
• Inversion is used here for dramatic effect, placing the auxiliary verb "have" before the subject "I".
 
• The correct grammatical structure is "Never have I ever...".

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Did I:** Is incorrect as it does not match the present perfect tense required in this context.
 
• **Has I:** Is grammatically incorrect as "has" should not be used with the subject "I".
 
• **I have:** Is incorrect because it does not follow the inversion structure used for emphasis.

questions.question:
The sentence below contains errors. Select the option with the correct use of tenses.

Your father will waiting for you when you reach home.

options.text: Your father should waiting for you when you reach home.
Your father will be waiting for you when you reach home.
Your father would waiting for you when you reach home.
Your father waiting for you when you reach home.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. Your father will be waiting for you when you reach home.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence uses an incorrect form of the future progressive tense** ("will waiting").**
 
• The correct form of the future progressive tense is **"will be waiting."**
 
• The other options (should waiting, would waiting, waiting) are not grammatically correct and do not fit the context of the sentence.

Correct sentence: *Your father will be waiting for you when you reach home*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Future Progressive Tense:**

 
 
• **Usage:** The future progressive tense is used to describe an action that will be ongoing at a specific point in the future.
 
• **Form:** Subject + will be + present participle (verb + -ing).
 
• **Example:** She will be studying when you arrive.
